classes.name: Round-1 mandatory amendments
classes.boundary: D1a reconciliation, excerpt/archive deletion, Doctor carve-out, Collector profile, append semantics, lifecycle replacement, and test oracles
classes.disposition: MOSTLY DISCHARGED. D1a is stated consistently: only a terminated unmatched child is ghost and a live unmatched child is pending; no session-existence birth rule remains. Phase 1 authorizes no excerpts. Archive/move/copy machinery is gone. Doctor scope is expressly locator-minimal. Collector persistence is expressly a package-owned public-contract amendment. Raw argv is replaced by non-content shape plus reference digests. The unsupported number is gone. ADR 0048/0049 are split. The activation fact replaces rather than accompanies ADR 0019's deleted lifecycle trace. Tests now require distinct correlation IDs and complete non-interleaved appends. The remaining defect is source authority in ADR 0049, adjudicated separately below.

classes.name: User stories 1–6
classes.boundary: Short launch, pre-dispatch fact, activation reconciliation, stdin discipline, canonical pointer, direct-home sessions
classes.disposition: SOUND under D1a/D3a. These stories now describe observable behavior without an existence-based ghost rule or archive mechanism.

classes.name: User story 7 and fact provenance
classes.boundary: Which record surface is authoritative for transcript, dispatch, and activation facts
classes.disposition: AMEND. The issue correctly requires each fact to carry its writing side/time, but ADR 0049 still says without qualification that “session 是正本，账本是索引.” A session cannot be canonical for the pre-dispatch fact, and a ghost may have no admitted session fact at all. State instead: the session is canonical for transcript/content; each producer-authored ledger event is canonical for its non-content dispatch or activation fact; correlation and pointers join those sources; the ledger copies no content bytes.

classes.name: User stories 8–9 and 11–15
classes.owner: Launcher projection, machine home, package distribution, and shared envelope
classes.boundary: Non-content retention, enumerability, npm consumers, no consumer-repo footprint, substrate-only scope, activation authorship, pending/ghost distinction
classes.disposition: SOUND. They are narrowed to first-phase facts and pointers, preserve caller composition, make no statistics claim, and do not recreate a Recorder scanner/schema/content archive.

classes.name: D4c identity semantics
classes.boundary: Root-commit fingerprint, empty repositories, forks, rewritten history, shallow clones, multiple roots, and non-Git calls
classes.disposition: OWNER DECISION STILL REQUIRED. A root commit identifies a history lineage, not a repository instance, and the current universal “cannot split” claim is false. Silent split constructions include: history rewriting/filtering that changes the root object ID; a shallow clone whose apparent root is the shallow boundary; changing clone depth; and adding/removing an unrelated history when the lexicographically least member of the root set changes. Silent merge constructions include independent clones/forks sharing the same root. Non-Git explicit keys permit typo-based splitting and contradict ADR 0048's unqualified “键不取外部输入.” Most seriously, all empty repositories have the same blank key: their pre-commit records either merge in one blank book or require an unstated provisional identity; after the first commit, immutable blank-key events and later fingerprint-key events split one repository unless an additional rebinding/migration mechanism is authorized. The text does not govern that transition.

classes.name: ADR 0047 fitness
classes.boundary: Pre-dispatch correlation fact × post-admission envelope fact and D1a finality
classes.disposition: SOUND. It is one hard-to-reverse decision, house-style short, and consistent with ADR 0010, 0018, 0019, and 0042.

classes.name: ADR 0048 fitness

However it omits the issue's multi-root and non-Git dispositions, states derived/no-external-input identity without the issue's non-Git exception, and does not govern blank-to-first-root continuity or the root-changing cases. Those are material semantics of its hard-to-reverse key decision, not Apply-local field spelling.

classes.name: ADR 0049 fitness

classes.disposition: AMEND. Zero copied content/excerpts, dumb append, and infrastructure-failure semantics are corpus-consistent with ADR 0036/0042/0043. arguments.note: Authority does not converge yet. All round-1 non-D4 repairs are materially present, but D4c as written cannot simultaneously promise a root-derived true key, a blank key before first commit, append-only records, and books that never split or merge. ADR 0049 also needs the already-required per-fact source-authority qualification.

decisionGate.question: Choose the governing identity semantics and amend issue #78/ADR 0048/tests accordingly. Which guarantee is intended when root identity is absent or changes?
options: D4c-A — Lineage books: keep the root fingerprint as the sole true key; explicitly accept that forks/clones merge, root rewrites/shallow boundaries/root-set changes split, and pre-commit records remain in an unassigned blank book. Narrow all “cannot split” claims to rename/worktree cases and qualify non-Git external keys.

D4c-B — Continuous repository books: authorize a persistent alias/rebinding mechanism for blank→first-root and old-root→new-root transitions, define conflict behavior, and test continuity. Root fingerprint remains the canonical lineage key, but the added mapping is an acknowledged mechanism and fresh clones/forks still share lineage unless separately decided.

D4c-C — Stable-key-only recording: retain root fingerprint as the sole key but do not launch/record project-book invocations for empty repositories, shallow repositories, non-Git directories, or unresolved multi-root transitions. This removes ambiguous rebinding at the cost of narrowing supported scope.

D4d — Repository-instance books: supersede D4c with a stable instance identity distinct from root history, and separately define clone/fork and non-Git behavior. This preserves per-instance continuity but abandons root fingerprint as the sole true key.

decisionGate.question:
AUTHORITY RULING — round-1 non-D4 orders are discharged: D1a is consistent; session-existence ghost language, excerpts, raw argv, archive, unsupported number, and parallel lifecycle trace are gone; Collector is explicitly amended to persist sessions; Doctor is locator-minimal; append failure, correlation uniqueness, and non-interleaved append oracles are present. ADR 0047 is fit. ADR 0048/0049 are correctly split and short. One non-owner amendment remains: ADR 0049 must qualify “session 是正本，账本是索引”: the session is canonical only for transcript/content; each producer event is canonical for its non-content dispatch or activation fact; correlation/pointers join them; no content is copied.

D4c is not sound as universal no-split law. A root commit identifies lineage, not repository instance. Books split when history rewrite/filtering changes the root, when a shallow boundary/depth changes, or when adding/removing unrelated history changes the lexicographically least root. Forks/clones sharing a root merge. A non-Git typo splits because its key is external, contradicting ADR 0048’s unqualified no-external-input claim. Empty repositories are the blocking contradiction: all have blank key, so pre-commit records either merge in one blank book or require an unstated provisional identity; after first commit, append-only blank-key events and fingerprint-key events split one repository unless rebinding is authorized. ADR 0048 must include the selected multi-root/non-Git/empty/root-change semantics. Tests must add observable oracles for those dispositions, especially continuity of pre-commit records. All other user stories, implementation decisions, scope, and Recorder red lines are sound.
